To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prototypic innate T cells and innate lymphoid cells are programmed by the same transcriptional network.
a network of transcription factors programs IL-17 production by innate-like lymphocytes in both the thymus, and the intestinal mucosa, independently of the anatomical location.
the transcription factors SOX13, SOX4 and TCF1/LEF1 program the development of innate lymphoid cells that produce IL-17 and IL-22.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of innate-like Tγδ17 effector cell differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms that govern T cell lineage specification.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of innate lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCF1 and the SOX proteins are essential in the development of innate lymphoid cells.

the TCF1/LEF1/SOX13/SOX4 quartet of transcription factors programs innate sources of interleukin 17 (IL- 17), independent of anatomical origin, and that the T cell lineage specifier TCF1 also controls the generation of IL 22 producing NKp46( + ) ILCs in the gut and restrains cytokine production by LTi-like effectors.
the transcription factors TCF1, LEF1, SOX4 and Sox13, in concert, control the development of Tγδ17, NKp46+ ILC22 and LTi cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a gene regulatory network of transcription factors programs the development and function of innate lymphoid cells.

the HMG transcription factor quartet SOX4, 13, TCF-1, and LEFI programs IL-17 production in innate-like Tγδ cells, and that the transcription factor TCF-1 programs IL-17 and IL-22 in innate lymphoid cells.
the HMG box transcription factor quartet of SOX4, 13, 1, and LEFs program the innate-like γδ and ILC17 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional network that programs IL-17 production by innate cells in the thymic and gut compartments is remarkably similar.
the same transcription factor network programs innate lymphoid cells in different anatomical compartments to produce IL-17.
a network of HMG box transcription factors programs the innate-like γδ17 T cells to produce interleukin-22 (IL-17) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) cytokines.
